key_reasoning.reason: Production changes span several subsystems: the SSO sign-in gate (sso.auth-gate.ts) and detached login lock (sso.detached-login.ts); the SSO proxy plugins (sso-auth, sso-session-expiry, sso.session-sync, credential-refresh); the session cookie-auth module with its superseded-credentials check; the metrics sync client, processor and types; the hook CLI command (hook.ts); the shared BaseProcessor classes; the codex, opencode and pi incremental-sync processors; and DesktopTelemetryRuntime. cookie-auth and the superseded-credentials check are shared by several sync paths.

No exact precedent for the new behaviour: a last-sign-in stamp carried across lock takeovers and scoped per URL, a TTL-cached superseded-credentials check shared through a WeakMap, and replay of superseded requests with fresh cookies. The code is concurrency-sensitive (a lock file shared across processes, atomic lock rewrites, orphaned tmp-file sweeping, in-flight de-duplication) and touches authentication and credential handling (cookies, auth-status marker, sign-in triggering). The tests cover many edge and race cases, with new dedicated lock, marker and superseded test files. Bumped from L to XL for the auth and concurrency red flags. A wrong decision either opens a second browser sign-in or suppresses a genuine re-auth prompt.

37 files changed (18 production, 19 test) across more than 10 directories under src/providers, src/agents, src/cli, src/telemetry and tests/integration. Diffstat is +3412/-236 (about 1,000 production lines). Count alone puts this at XXL, although most of the volume is tests.

Service layer (auth gate, credential refresh, metrics sync processors); API/CLI layer (hook command, proxy plugins); Infrastructure (cross-process lock file, auth-status marker, detached browser process spawning); External (CodeMie platform metrics endpoint and SSO login). The cross-process lock file and credential-store reads are persistence-adjacent but there is no schema change or migration, so this stays at L rather than XL.

red_flags_applied: Technical Risk bumped from L to XL: affects authentication and credential handling (SSO cookies, auth-status marker, sign-in gating) and involves cross-process lock concurrency.

Technical Risk: the closest pattern is the existing detached-login lock and auth-status marker, which did not cover the superseded-credentials and per-URL sign-in stamp cases. Enumerated edge and race cases in the tests add to the risk.
Component Scope held at XL: touches shared utilities (cookie-auth, the BaseProcessor classes) used by several agent sync paths.
